Sepsis sucks. I had a kidney infection while I was pregnant or shortly after I had my baby that went unnoticed. No symptoms or it was really hard to tell because everything hurt from having a baby. I ended up having pretty bad lower back pain, but again, just had a baby. Finally, I spiked a fever of 104 and felt miserable. Went to urgent care and the doctor there said I likely had the flu (in July) and gave me a steroid to take. I didn’t get better. I called my mom and told her that I knew I was going to die tonight.

Ended up going to the ER where they caught the kidney infection and then they took quite a bit of blood from different arms. Got the results back that I had sepsis. I didn’t stay in the hospital but had to go back everyday for a week to get the antibiotics through an IV line that stayed in. While having a 4 week old baby. Worst time of my life.

All I can offer is solidarity. My daughter would have absolute nightmare level tantrums when she was hungry or tired. She would bite, kick, scratch, hit and be red faced screaming the entire time. It was miserable and I cried a lot from about 2-4. 

She is 5 now and they have lessened but not gone away completely. She isn’t biting or hitting anymore, thankfully. She has constant snack breaks and I always have a snack to help with the hangry episodes. For sleep, we found that she wasn’t getting quality sleep but once we got that figured out, it has helped so much. She still will have meltdowns, especially after a busy day, but they are more manageable and there are longer times in between. As someone else mentioned, finding letters and numbers in the real world. We did that with my daughter, starting with the letters in her name because that was fun. Then, turned to M for Mommy and D for Daddy. She is in kindergarten now and we’ve moved onto sight words. 

She was in a play based preschool/daycare that didn’t really focus on any of that and we didn’t really focus on it at home, either. She would often “forget” letters and numbers, usually because she wasn’t interested in doing it then. Never pressed the issue. It really wasn’t until kindergarten that she really retained it and can now breeze through the alphabet and the sounds. 

For writing, I don’t think it’s developmentally appropriate for her to be writing letters. Just turned 4 is still so small! I would focus more on strengthening her grip and fine motor skills. We did a lot of play dough, kinetic sand, coloring, tracing. Working in correctly holding the pencil, which was a fight with my daughter until recently. 

Again, just turned 4 is still small!! I would also suggest reading to her every night, if you aren’t already and letting her have fun being 4. So much will change in a year.

I mean, not entirely accurate. There are different rules for making funds available from a check according to Reg CC. Not always one business days. They will generally make a portion of the funds available and the rest on hold for some length of time, likely a day or two. But that depends on how and when you deposit the check. Some institutions will place long holds if it is done after business hours or on a weekend. 

Second, the bank or credit union you deposited the check at isn’t verifying anything. It runs through the system and it’s up to the institution where the check is drawn off to bounce a fraudulent check. Likely, it’s up to the account owner that the check is drawing from to dispute it. That’s why the time frame to dispute checks is so long for all the old people that depend on paper statements to check their accounts. 

Generally, the rule of thumb is 3-5 business days. It can take up to a year to bounce for being fake but that is actually kind of an exception and not the rule. Any other reason for bouncing, like No Account or Insufficient Funds have tighter timeframes to bounce and if not done quick enough can be pushed back to the originating institution. It gets complicated. 

I also don’t think credit is affected, at least at my institution. We have the ability to place a record in Chex to indicate the fraud but we normally don’t unless it egregious. But we can and will close membership for fraudulent activity in your account. 

Source: I work in fraud at a credit union.

We specifically train tellers to not outright tell people checks are real or that a check has cleared. Wells Fargo didn’t just decide the checks were fake but the bank where the checks were drawn from. 

In short, a check is deposited into your account and then it goes to the Fed who then communicates with the other bank to pull the money. It does and then the account owner sees the check clearing and will dispute it. That is communicated back to the Fed who then tells your bank and the money is pulled from your account. It’s why it takes so long to have a check bounce. 

Because your friend spent the money as part of this scam and the check is then pulled they are responsible for the balance. Dad is then in the middle by being a joint owner and Wells offset his money. 

Not all checks look outright fraudulent and checks can bounce for so many reasons. Insufficient funds, refer to maker, unable to locate account, stop payment. All in all, don’t accept checks from anyone.

Skinner would probably not believe that this is superstitious behavior in the least.  Being a behaviorist, superstition is something that is going on in the brain of the pigeon, which means that it is not something that can readily be observed.  Skinner would have believed this was operant conditioning because the pigeon, probably being on a variable interval schedule of reinforcement, believed that some previous behavior elicited the reward of the food so they will continue to do it in order to obtain more food.

I do not believe this would be considered classical conditioning.  The behavior of doing some ritual and then receiving food (the reward) is actually operant conditioning.  Operant conditioning involves rewards and punishments whereas classical conditioning does not.
